2013_044_011513org_regmtg.paragraph: Troy School District's Board of Education held its Organizational Meeting at 7:00 p.m. and a Regular Meeting at 7:15 p.m. on January 15, 2013 at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois. The organizational half elected officers for terms until December 31, 2013, appointed Mark S. Rajter, Assistant Superintendent for Business Services, as Treasurer for January through December 2013, and adopted a depository and investment resolution listing the district's depository banks and investment institutions. The regular half carried the November 2012 Treasurer's Report, reporting total disbursements in the period of $4,899,890.37, and awarded bids of $28,115.00 to J. B. Electrical Company and $250,796.00 to Konica Minolta.

**Meeting**

Troy School District Board of Education, Tuesday, January 15, 2013. Organizational Meeting at 7:00 p.m., Regular Meeting at 7:15 p.m., Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098. Superintendent Barbara A. Fowler, Ph.D. Trustees named in the roll-call sequences: Underwood, Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Miletti, Philippart, Schmidt.

**Organizational actions**

- Judy Holmes appointed temporary secretary; four votes required to elect an officer. President, Vice President and Secretary elected for terms until December 31, 2013.
- Mark S. Rajter, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, appointed Treasurer for January through December 2013 as a nonvoting officer.
- Depository and investment resolution for January through December 2013: depository banks (Bank of America, Bank of New York, JP Morgan Chase, Citizen's Bank, Comerica, Fifth Third, MILAF and PFM Securities through Fifth Third, PNC) and a list of investment institutions, investing under Board Policy D-1103 and Section 380.1223(1)(h) of the Revised School Code. Health-care claim checks over $10,000 need a second handwritten signature from Jasen Witt or Monica Papasian.
- Superintendent continued as Deputy Secretary; Judy Holmes designated to post meeting notices; 2013 meeting calendar adopted.

**Recognition and consent agenda**

Fall Senior Scholar Athletes, honored for a 3.5 cumulative grade point average while participating in an athletic program, and fall All-State athletes Zachary Doepke, Brett Forman, Mitch Guitar, Nicole Hahn, Max Klitzke, Jennifer Yang and Richard Zang. Board recognition is an ink drawing titled "Transformation" by International Academy-East student Madeleine Chong, matted with art teacher Sandy LewAllen. The consent agenda covered minutes of the December 4, 2012 meeting and December 11, 2012 workshop and the November 2012 Treasurer's Report.

**Personnel, curriculum, business and policy**

Probationary contracts for the remainder of 2012-2013 for Renee Boogren (1.0 FTE Science, Niles Community High School) and Nichelle Dowgiert (1.0 FTE ASD, Athens High School). Schools of Choice resolutions under Sections 105 and 105c of the State School Aid Act of 1979 as amended by Public Act 300 of 1996 for 2013-2014: 100 nonresident kindergarten and 30 nonresident first-grade seats, and 25 nonresident sixth- through eighth-grade seats at Baker Middle School. Bids: UPS replacement at Morse Elementary to J. B. Electrical Company for $28,115.00, and 22 multi-function copiers to Konica Minolta for $250,796.00 with a five-year service agreement estimated at $44,250 per year, both from the 2012-2013 General Fund. Dr. Fowler reported on the 2012-2013 Superintendent's goals and November 2013 bond preparation, and a first reading of revised Board Policy K-1303, Commercial Advertising, closed the agenda.

**Setting.** Board packet for the Troy School District (Oakland County, Michigan) Board of Education Organizational Meeting and Regular Meeting of Tuesday, January 15, 2013 - the Organizational Meeting at 7:00 p.m. and the Regular Meeting at 7:15 p.m., both at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098. District letterhead lists 4400 Livernois and 248.823.4000; meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) and streamed at http://vimeo.com/troyschools. Public communication allows one-half hour each for agenda and non-agenda items, three minutes per speaker.

**Organizational meeting.** Superintendent Barbara A. Fowler, Ph.D. notes that the previous year's president chairs until a president is elected, that Judy Holmes serves as temporary secretary, and that four votes are required for election. President, Vice President and Secretary were elected for terms until December 31, 2013, roll call rotating through the trustees: Underwood, Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Miletti, Philippart, Schmidt. Item 6.B appoints Mark S. Rajter, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, as Treasurer for January through December 2013, a nonvoting officer appointed annually under Board policy.

**Depositories and investments (Item 6.C).** The resolution for January through December 2013 designates depository banks: Bank of America, Bank of New York, JP Morgan Chase Bank, Citizen's Bank, Comerica Bank, Fifth Third Bank, MILAF (Michigan Liquid Asset Fund Plus) managed by PFM Asset Management, Inc. through Fifth Third Bank, PFM Securities, Inc. through Fifth Third Bank, and PNC Bank. Checks carry Treasurer Rajter's facsimile signature, with emergency handwritten signature by Rajter or Superintendent Fowler on the Bank of America General Fund and Payroll accounts, handwritten signature by Troy Career Center management on PNC Bank accounts, and, on the Bank of America health-claims account, a second handwritten signature from Jasen Witt, Assistant Superintendent for Human Resources, or Monica Papasian, Finance Director, for checks over $10,000; a Comerica Bank flexible-spending account is drawn by ACH debit to Next Generation Enrollment, Inc. Investments follow Board Policy D-1103, and the Treasurer may combine money from more than one fund under subsection (1)(h) of Section 380.1223 of the Revised School Code. The investment institution list adds Charter One Bank, Flagstar Bancorp and Morgan Stanley Smith Barney. Related items continue the Superintendent as Deputy Secretary for 2013, designate Judy Holmes to post meeting notices, and adopt the 2013 calendar of 7:00 p.m. regular meetings at the Services Building and 6:00 p.m. workshops at the Administrative Center, with the June 4 meeting set as the Annual Recognition Meeting at Athens High School, the March 19 workshop at GROW, and the next organizational meeting on January 14, 2014.

**Recognition.** Senior Scholar Athletes are honored for maintaining a 3.5 cumulative grade point average while participating in an athletic program, on a Troy High and Athens High roster. Fall 2012 All-State athletes, whose biographies Mr. Jolly read, are Zachary Doepke (boys soccer, Troy), Brett Forman (boys tennis, Troy, Mr. Tennis 2012), freshman Mitch Guitar (boys soccer, Troy), Nicole Hahn (volleyball, Troy), Max Klitzke (boys soccer, Athens), Jennifer Yang (girls golf, Athens) and Richard Zang (boys tennis, Athens), with coaches Brian Zawislak, Brian Miska, Vince Muscat, Todd Heugh, Dan Cooper and Andrew Shipp. Board recognition is an ink drawing titled "Transformation" by International Academy-East student Madeleine Chong, matted and framed with art teacher Sandy LewAllen, plus a laminated year-long calendar.

**Minutes.** The December 4, 2012 meeting was called to order at 5:45 p.m. by President Philippart, with Edmunds, Hauff, Miletti, Schmidt and Underwood present and Mrs. Fleming absent. Resolution 12-103 took the Board into closed session on negotiations under the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c), carried 6-0; closed session began at 5:47 p.m. and the meeting reconvened at 7:09 p.m. Resolution 12-104 approved the November 13, 2012 minutes and October 2012 Treasurer's Report; Resolution 12-105 approved new hires Angela Locken and Sherry Richardson; Resolution 12-106 accepted the audited 2012 financial statements presented by Plante Moran auditor Teresa Pollock, who called the unqualified opinion the highest level and free of errors under GAAP. Mr. Witt, with Carrie Sekich, Aaron Maelipard and Joe Duda, presented the Teacher Evaluation Appraisal Model (TEAM). Adjournment was 8:17 p.m.; minutes submitted by Secretary Todd Miletti. The December 11, 2012 workshop ran 6:02 p.m. to 8:40 p.m. with the full Board present and covered Board fiduciary responsibility to the Foundation, the 2011-2014 District Technology Plan, Schools of Choice 105 and 105C, Board Policy K-1303 and bond issue discussion.

**Personnel, Schools of Choice and bids.** Probationary contracts for the remainder of 2012-2013 are recommended for Renee Boogren, 1.0 FTE Science at Niles Community High School (Marquette University, Gannon University, M.A. Wayne State University 1991, Michigan Professional Certificate September 2012, resident of Troy) and Nichelle Dowgiert, 1.0 FTE ASD at Athens High School (Oakland University 2005, M.A. Saginaw Valley State University May 2012, Michigan Provisional Certificate June 2011, resident of Macomb). Schools of Choice resolutions under Sections 105 and 105c of the State School Aid Act of 1979, as amended by Public Act 300 of 1996, cover 2013-2014: 100 nonresident kindergarten and 30 nonresident first-grade students, both for districts within Oakland County and for districts whose intermediate school district is contiguous with Oakland ISD, plus 25 nonresident sixth- through eighth-grade students at Baker Middle School under each section. Bids for the Morse Elementary UPS replacement went to four potential bidders with three responding, were reviewed by Kenneth Miller, Executive Director of Operations, and Richard Bracci, Senior Vice President, IDS, and the award goes to J. B. Electrical Company for $28,115.00 from the 2012-2013 General Fund. Ken Crawford, Interim Acting Director of Technology, and Mark Rajter recommend 22 Konica Minolta multi-function copiers for $250,796.00 with a five-year service agreement estimated at $44,250 annually; Merri Lynn Colligan identified the worst machines in fall 2012, Konica has indicated parts are no longer available, and the district used an existing Livingston Educational Service Agency pricing agreement with Konica Minolta that began in 2010 and is valid until 2/12/15. Purchase runs $25,000 less than a 36-month lease-to-own contract, and the .0039 cents-per-copy service rate covers maintenance, repairs and toner. The schedule lists Bizhub 951 units at $13,364 for most buildings, a Bizhub 1052 at $17,624 and Bizhub 223 units at $3,000 for IAE and the Career Center, Bizhub 552 units at $5,580 at Services, and a Bizhub C35 at $2,188 for B & G at a 0.012 rate, with annual copy volume of 11,329,068.

**Superintendent's goals and bond preparation.** Dr. Fowler's 2012-2013 update centers on increasing the number of students college and career ready in literacy, mathematics, science and social studies. Five cohort groups of seven to eight fourth-grade teachers give 100 percent participation in coordinator-facilitated teacher labs, alongside work with Carol Jago, Frank Serafini and Lester Laminack and 24 volunteer high school teachers in Hi-Class content literacy. Mathematics covers Smarter Balanced alignment, an elementary committee piloting three programs for spring recommendation, and Big Ideas Mathematics in grades 6 and 7 with grade 8 next fall. Science introduced the claim-evidence-reasoning framework through Darin Stockdill on August 29th, with 30-minute sessions at all 12 elementary schools and PASCO training for physics teachers; social studies targets 24 teachers trained in grades 6-12; and a math support class adds three hours of instruction per week for middle school students. Bond preparation for a November 2013 election includes a completed TMP Architecture facility assessment of site, roofing, plumbing/HVAC and electrical, a district-wide technology assessment, a nine-year bus replacement schedule, site visits completed by January 18, 2013, a community survey run January 7-10 and completed January 10, 2013, results to be reviewed at the January 22nd workshop, and the bond amount to be presented February 5th. A cost analysis of the current finance and human resources software puts cost per student at $12 or more; the district intends to move to Oakland Schools' Tyler Munis solution along with 22 other Oakland County districts over the next four fiscal years, subsidized for the first five years and approximately $10 per student thereafter, with final commitment letters due late Fall 2013.

**Policy K-1303.** A first reading of revisions to Board Policy K-1303, Commercial Advertising, in the K-1300 series on advertising and distribution of materials in the schools, was reviewed by the Board's attorney for compliance with state law, the Open Meetings Act and the Revised School Code. The policy bars commercial material causing substantial and material interference with normal school activities from being displayed on district-owned property without written consent of the superintendent or designee, permits display on personal vehicles parked on school property, and restricts school and contracted personnel from using district resources, technology, e-mail and student or parent contact information for commercial purposes. Adopted May 3, 1976; revised January 16, 1979, April 21, 1998, April 20, 2010 and June 19, 2012.
